Used in English since 13th century. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # One which receives or entertains a [[guest]], socially, commercially, or officially. #: {{ux|en|A good '''host''' is always considerate of the guest’s needs.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Troilus and Cressida|III|iii|passage=Time is like a fashionable '''host''', / That slightly shakes his parting guest by the hand.}} # One that provides a facility for an event. # A person or organization responsible for [[run]]ning an [[event]]. #: {{ux|en|Our company is '''host''' of the annual conference this year.}} # A [[moderator]] or [[master of ceremonies]] for a [[performance]]. #: {{syn|en|presenter|q=UK}} #: {{ux|en|The '''host''' was terrible, but the acts themselves were good.}} # {{lb|en|multiplicity}} The [[primary]] [[member]] of a {{l|en|system|id=set of headmates}}, typically the member who {{l|en|front|id=be in control of the body|fronts}} most often. # {{lb|en|computing|Internet}} Any computer attached to a [[network]]. # {{lb|en|ecology}} A [[cell]] or [[organism]] which [[harbor]]s another organism or biological entity, usually a [[parasite]]. #: {{ux|en|Viruses depend on the '''host''' that they infect in order to be able to reproduce.}} # {{lb|en|evolution|genetics}} An organism bearing certain [[genetic]] material, with respect to its cells. #: {{ux|en|The so-called junk DNA is known, so far, to provide no apparent benefit to its '''host'''.}} # A [[paid]] [[male]] [[companion]] offering [[conversation]] and in some cases [[sex]], as in certain types of [[bar]] in [[Japan]]. =====Hyponyms===== * X, Plugson of Undershot||Why, Plugson, even thy own '''host''' is all in mutiny: Cotton is conquered; but the ‘bare backs’ — are worse covered than ever!}} #* {{RQ:Tolkien Return of the King|chapter=chapter 4, The Field of Cormallen|text=All about the '''hosts''' of Mordor raged.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=Carlos Parada|title=Hesione 2|sectionurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20011218163821/http://homepage.mac.com/cparada/GML/Hesione2.html|section=Greek Mythology Link |passage=the invading '''host''' that had sailed from Hellas in more than one thousand ships was of an unprecedented size.}} # A large number of items; a large [[inventory]]. #: {{ux|en|The dealer stocks a '''host''' of parts for my Model A.}} #: {{ux|en|There are a '''host''' of reasons for this decision.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1802|author=w:William Wordsworth|title=I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud |passage=I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A '''host''', of golden daffodils; {{...}}}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1836|journal=The Mirror of Literature, Amusement, and Instruction |passage=A short time since, some friends drinking tea one summer evening at their residence near Maidenhead, with all the windows of the drawing-room open, there suddenly burst in a '''host''' of small flies, which covered the table and the furniture {{...}}}} #* {{quote-web|en|author=w:Phil McNulty|title=[[w:Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]] 1 – 2 [[w:England national football team|England]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190421215852/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44434276|archivedate=21 April 2019|work=w:BBC Sport|date=18 June 2018|passage=England ran Tunisia ragged in that spell but were punished for missing a '''host''' of chances when {{w|Ferjani Sassi}} equalised from the penalty spot against the run of play after {{w|Kyle Walker}} was penalised for an elbow on {{w|Fakhreddine Ben Youssef}}.}} =====Derived terms===== * {{l|en|heavenly host}} * {{l|en|Lord of Hosts}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|multitude of people arrayed as an army}} * Arabic: * Aramaic: * Armenian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Comorian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Old Norse: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|рать|f}}, {{t+|ru|во́йско|n}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Ugaritic: * Ukrainian: * Vietnamese: * Volapük: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|large number of items}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * Hungarian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|мно́жество|n}} * Swedish: * Ukrainian: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== {{ety|en|id=from sacrifice-referent origins|:inh|enm:host}} From {{inh|en|enm|host}}, {{m|enm|oyst}}, {{m|enm|oist}}, {{m|enm|ost}}, from {{der|en|fro|hoiste}}, from {{der|en|la|hostia||sacrificial victim}}. {{doublet|en|hostie}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} #
